To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a wide range of algorithms and methodologies to segment and classify point clouds.

1) the segmentation of 3D point cloud data into regions with similar characteristics is a challenging task, 2) the classification of 3D objects is a complex task, 3) there is a need of new methodologies to improve the segmentation and classification of 3d objects.
the most popular algorithms to segment and label 3D point-cloud are based on the region growing method and on statistical analysis of the point-cloud.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms for 3D segmentation and classification of large point clouds, and with the application of these methods to cultural heritage.

the following questions: What are the different methods to segment and classify point clouds? What is the performance of the different algorithms? What are the advantages and disadvantages? What are the open research issues?
the development of new methods and algorithms to segment, classify and label point clouds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no general algorithms that work well on every kind of data.
there is no single best solution to segment and classify point clouds and the best approach is to combine different methodologies to obtain a more robust and reliable solution.
segmentation and classification of 3D point cloud are still open issues, even though many solutions have been proposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to obtain a good result, it is necessary to use a combination of algorithms and to apply them in a specific order.
segmentation is a very important step for classification.
, despite the large amount of algorithms available in literature, the problem of segmenting and classifying 3D point cloud is still open.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single algorithm that works best in all cases and that there is no algorithm that is the best one in all the different fields of application.

, despite the large number of algorithms proposed in the literature, there is still the need for a general purpose segmentation and classification algorithm that is fast, accurate, easy to use, flexible and able to work on large datasets.
the state-of-the-art algorithms are not yet ready to provide a full automatic solution for 3D point cloud processing.
